questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

Sarah __writes a book__ that became a bestseller.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**wrote a book**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, '**wrote a book**' should be used instead of '**write a book**'.
 
• This is because the **sentence** is in** the past tense, **and the event of Sarah's book becoming a bestseller has already happened in **the past**.
 
• Therefore, the verb should also be in the past tense to maintain grammatical consistency.
 
• "**Wrote**" is the past tense form of "**write**", and it correctly indicates that Sarah has already completed the task of writing the book.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• Option 2**, "will write a book"**, is in the future tense and is not appropriate for the given sentence because it suggests that the book is yet to be written, whereas the sentence is discussing an event that has already happened.
 
• Option 4, **"had write a book",** is not grammatically correct. The past participle form of "write" is "written", and the past perfect tense would require "had written". However, the past perfect tense is not necessary in this sentence as there is no need to show a past action that occurred before another past action.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Sarah __**wrote a book**__ that became a bestseller.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate idiom from the following options that can substitute the underlined part of the given sentence.**

Dheerubai, a source of inspiration to the present generation, __started life very poor and then later in life became very rich__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Went from rags to riches'.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined part **"started life very poor and then later in life became very rich"** is** "went from rags to riches".**
 
• This idiom means **to start life very poor and become rich later. **
 
• Origin of this idiom:
 
 
• The idiom** "rags to riches" **originates from the idea that someone who starts with nothing, symbolized by "**rags**," can achieve great wealth and success, symbolized by "**riches**," through hard work and determination.
 
• It is often associated with the American Dream, the idea that anyone can achieve success and prosperity through hard work and determination, regardless of social status or background.
 
• The phrase is believed to have been first coined by Horatio Alger Jr., an American writer of children's books in the 19th century, who wrote many stories about young people from humble backgrounds who became successful through hard work and perseverance.

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** Went from rags to riches.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Dragged his feet: **to delay or to act slowly on something
 
• **Got it off his chest:** to tell someone about something that has been worrying you, so that you feel better
 
• **Felt the pinch: **to experience financial difficulties.

questions.question:

Stevie loved a good mystery novel.

options.text: A good mystery novel was being loved by Stevie.
A good mystery novel was loved by Stevie.
A good mystery novel had been loved by Stevie.
A good mystery novel is loved by Stevie.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**A good mystery novel was loved by Stevie.​'**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it to Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'Stevie'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'A good mystery'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'loved' will be changed into 'was loved'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *A good mystery novel was loved by Stevie.*
